North Little Rock’s class of ’26 graduates
424 students graduated from North Little Rock High School on May 18th. The class included 90 honor
graduates. Above, North Little Rock High School Senior Taniea Johnson watches her fellow classmates give
their commencement speeches on the large Jumbotron at UA Little Rock Jack Stephen’s center. JEFFREY SMITH/Leader photos

 115 students graduate from Lonoke High School
 Lonoke High School held graduation on Friday at the Gina Cox Center. There were 115 students graduating
 32 with honors. The graduates had an estimated $1.25 million in scholarship offers. The valedictorian was
 Karr Graham. The salutatorians were Collins Gentry and Walker Smith.

RESOLUTION NO. 28 OF 2019

A RESOLUTION TO ADOPT THE ANNUAL OPERATING BUDGET FOR
CALENDAR YEAR 2020; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann. § 14-58-201 et seq. requires the City of Cabot to adopt an
annual budget on or before February 1st of each year.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The annual budget for calendar year 2020 attached hereto as Exhibit “A”
and incorporated herein by this reference, is hereby adopted. A copy of said budget shall be filed
in the Office of the City Clerk and shall be available for inspection and copying by any person
during normal office hours.

SECTION 2: Consistent with the requirements of Ark. Code Ann. § 14-58-203, no
funds of the City of Cabot shall be spent in such a manner that would (1) result in funds raised by
taxes levied for specific purposes being diverted to another purpose; or (2) result in prejudicing
any creditor of the city.

SECTION 3: No expenditure of appropriated funds shall be made from any fund other
than the fund specified for the expenditure by this Resolution or an amendment thereto.

SECTION 4: This Resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after the date of

its passage.

 In 1976, I graduated from Cabot High School and then, attended Arkansas
 State University and UALR and received an AA degree in Agriculture and a
 BA in criminal justice.
 I graduated first in my class from the Arkansas Law Enforcement
 Academy, then served two years with the Cabot Police Department and
 twenty-eight years with the Little Rock Police Department, retiring in 2010.
 My duties with the LRPD included 21 years as security for UA Razorback
 football head coach and 8 years on Presidential Security for President
 Bill Clinton. My assignments at LRPD included patrol, special intelligence
 division, mounted patrol and special operations division. I served 20 years
 on the board of the LRPD Fraternal Order of Police and was elected 7
 terms as president and contract negotiator. I received the Arkansas Police
 Officer of the Year for lifesaving award.
 I am the past President of the Central Arkansas Cattlemen’s Association
 as well as State Board Representative. I served the Arkansas State Horse
 Show Association as Chairman for four terms. I served on the advisory
 board for War Memorial Stadium, the Arkansas State Fair and Livestock
 Show, Arkansas Ballet, Arkansas Special Olympics, Little Rock Marathon,
 Clinton Library opening, Cabot FFA and was a founding member and
 served two terms as president of the Cabot Panther Foundation. In 2019, I
 was inducted into the Cabot Panther Foundation Hall of Fame.
 After retirement, I re-entered the workforce and spent 3 years as Director
 of Emergency Services for Lonoke County.
 My wife, Dawn, spent 39 years with the Cabot School District, having retired as an elementary school principal. We have been married for 38
 years and have two adult children, Morgan and Jay. Morgan and her husband, Matt Yates, have triplet 4-year olds. Together we own and operate
 WoodLawn Ranch and Arena.
 I don’t consider myself a politician, but instead, a lifelong public servant. I hope to continue that service as the next elected county judge of our
 wonderful county. I assure you, no one will outwork me and I answer to the taxpayers of Lonoke County. I look forward to talking with the voters
 to share my goals and objectives and hearing new and fresh ideas, as well.
 THANK YOU FOR YOUR SUPPORT!
